title: Read and write square notation: 7² means 7 × 7 = 49, not 7 × 2

lesson.title: What the Little 2 Really Means

steps.say: You already know that a perfect square is a number that can be laid out as a perfect square array, like 49 counters in 7 rows of 7. Today we learn the shortcut way to write that, and the one little trap almost everyone falls into.

Here it is. Seven squared means a square that is 7 across and 7 down. So seven squared is seven times seven, which is forty nine. The little 2 up high tells you how many sevens are being multiplied together — two of them — it does not tell you to multiply by 2.

visual.caption: A 7 by 7 square made of 49 small squares

steps.say: Now the trap. Lots of people see three squared and say six, because they doubled instead of squaring. Watch what three squared really is: a square 3 across and 3 down. Count the little squares — nine, not six. Six would be three plus three. Squaring is three times three. Doubling and squaring are two different jobs.

visual.caption: A 3 by 3 square holding 9 small squares, not 6

steps.say: Let us go the other direction too. Say you are tiling a square patch of your backyard that is 8 tiles across and 8 tiles down. You could write 8 times 8, but the short way is 8 squared. And 8 squared is 8 times 8, which is sixty four tiles. Same picture, shorter writing.

visual.caption: An 8 by 8 tile patch with 64 tiles in total

steps.say: So here is the whole idea in one line: when you see a little 2, say the number times itself. Seven squared is seven times seven, forty nine. Never seven times two.

lesson.answer: A little 2 means multiply the number by itself: 7² = 7 × 7 = 49, not 14.

practice.question: A skate park in your town has a square concrete pad that measures 9 metres along each side. Write the number of square metres using square notation, then work out the value.
